20 ## The Elegance Law (locked by John — binding on this skill)
21 
22 Canonical text: `Skill Foundry/ELEGANCE.md`. Applies to ANY agent running this
23 skill on ANY host. If this block and a longer procedure below disagree, this
24 block wins.
25 
26 1. **Approvals are ≤200 words** — what changes in his world, the recommendation,
27    the one thing that gets worse. The artifact stays on disk and is named, not
28    pasted. An approval obtained with a longer block is VOID.
29 2. **Summaries are ≤150 words** — goal in one line, done / not done, ≤3 findings
30    ranked by consequence, the single next decision. Never rounds, waves, seats,
31    stamps, gate counts, or file inventories.
32 3. **Default to the lightest band, without asking.** A heavier tier requires the
33    first status line to NAME its trigger: irreversible or externally visible,
34    inputs unconverged, a prior failure in this exact area, or he asked for it.
35 4. **Needed-because line.** Any element he did not request carries one line:
36    "Needed because ___; dropping it costs ___." No line, no element.
37 5. **Show a cut.** ONE dry round ends a review loop — never a streak. Every plan
38    names something it removed; "nothing cut" is said aloud.
39 
40 **THE VERIFICATION LAW** (added 2026-08-15 after its FOURTH recurrence — each of
41 the first three was written into a journal and recurred anyway):
42 
43 6. **Verify the claim you actually made, on the surface he actually uses.**
44    "It's live / fixed / renders" is a claim about HIS screen. That the server
45    emits new bytes, that a build exited zero, or that assertions passed are
46    claims about something else. Render it and look at it.
47 7. **A symptom reported twice retires the first explanation.** Test the
48    hypothesis; never repeat it. An explanation that makes his report false
49    ("it's your cache", "it's a data issue") needs MORE evidence, not less.
50 8. **Prefer a mechanism to an instruction.** If the same instruction is given
51    every session, the instruction is the defect — build what removes it.
52 9. **A correction that lives only in a journal or a memory has not been made.**
53    Promote it to where it is loaded BEFORE the work starts.
54 
55 **Two laws these serve.** A gate that cannot see what the user sees is not a gate
56 — structure diffs are lints, and must be labelled as lints. And a guardrail is
57 never the whole product of a turn — if enforcement withholds output he already
58 paid for, show it anyway.

94 # Foreman
95 
96 Autonomous multi-wave build orchestrator (working title "code-execution-organizer").
97 Foreman is a Claude Code **skill** invoked in a project folder. Given that
98 project's *frozen* design + implementation-plan docs, it drives each
99 wave/sprint/section to done through fresh-context sub-agents, auto-advances to
100 the next wave, keeps the tree clean, prints running commentary, and **halts only
101 on a defined blocker set**.
102 
103 > **Tier definition (Heavy vs regular · stakes-gated cross-model · seat mapping) + invocation
104 > discipline (zero deliberation · the LOCKED global status table · run capture):** canonical in
105 > `AGENTS.md` (Foundry root on the author host; your install root in a distributed bundle) → "Skill tiers" / "Invocation discipline" / "Run capture".
106 > Trio build tier: `TRIO_TIER=heavy|standard` (standard is the build default). Do not re-define
107 > or deliberate any of it.
108 
109 > **Status (2026-08-24, consolidated — the ONE status block; verified currency lives in
110 > `Skill Foundry/PLAN.md`): PRODUCTION — ~15 real builds shipped** (aurora,
111 > researchPrime-upgrade, ramanujan, the Anchor rearchitecture 20/20 waves, most Foundry
112 > skills). Suite: `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"` (the bare directory form false-fails on
113 > fixture subdirs). The ground-truth gate is orchestrator-run (unforgeable); the JUDGE is a
114 > pure function, not an agent. Operationally hardened through 2026-07: async gate with
115 > per-minute heartbeat + on-disk plan rebind each iteration; classified gate timeouts
116 > (`[taxonomy:gate-timeout]`, child-tree kill, never a fake RED); per-wave scoped gates
117 > (0086); halt taxonomy prefixes on every reason; `review:degraded` honest seat-dropping
118 > (gate stays ground truth §5); EXECUTION-LOG.md orchestrator-appended on every GO.
119 > **Halt recovery:** `--clear-halt` on a vacuous halt is REFUSED unless code landed;
120 > `--clear-halt --force` re-enters EXECUTE with eyes open; a PLAN-AMENDMENT clear
121 > re-enters EXECUTE at iteration 0; resume re-proves GREEN.
122 > **NEVER run `git clean -fd` in a Foreman workspace** — two total-project-loss
123 > events (journals 0013/0042). Non-convergence uses `git stash` (recoverable);
124 > untracked deliverables are exactly what `git clean` destroys.
125 
126 ## What Foreman is / is NOT
127 
128 - **Is:** a loop that takes a frozen plan and drives it to done wave by wave —
129   EXECUTE -> ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW -> FIX -> RE-REVIEW until convergence, then
130   auto-advance, with logging, hygiene, commits, and running commentary. **(built — see `bin/`)**
131 - **Is NOT:** a planner. It never invents requirements, refactors for taste
132   outside the plan, or makes reserved architectural calls — those are **halts**.
133   This anti-scope-creep contract is its most important property.
134 
135 ## Topology (the load-bearing rule)
136 
137 Do **not** parallelize code-writing — coding is the least-parallelizable task and
138 parallel coders make conflicting implicit decisions (Anthropic + Cognition both
139 agree; see `research1-out/.../01-report.md` F1/F2).
140 
141 | Phase | Topology |
142 |---|---|
143 | EXECUTE | single-threaded linear agent per wave; compress when long |
144 | REVIEW | `REVIEWER_COUNT` (default 2) independent reviewers, **CONCURRENT** (default on), read-only, prompted to refute; **stakes-gated** — ordinary clean mid-run waves run 1, the full panel runs on the terminal wave / after fix iterations / `FOREMAN_FULL_REVIEW=1`; skipped entirely on RED intermediate iterations (the gate artifact IS the fix guidance) |
145 | FIX | single-threaded linear agent |
146 | JUDGE | a PURE FUNCTION (0 model calls); the **orchestrator-run ground-truth gate dominates** (§5) |
147 
148 `REVIEWER_COUNT` is one config var (default 2) — never hard-coded.
149 Independence comes from separate sub-agent calls, never multi-persona-in-one-generation.
150

153 ## §4 — Invocation / contract (the confirmation flow)
154 
155 On invocation, Foreman resolves the contract and **states it back for the user
156 to confirm before building**. The deterministic, no-guess part is implemented in
157 `bin/locate-plan.mjs` (which uses `bin/foreman-lib.mjs`):
158 
159 ```
160 node foreman/bin/locate-plan.mjs [projectDir]      # human-readable contract
161 node foreman/bin/locate-plan.mjs --json [projectDir]
162 ```
163 
164 Exit codes: `0` contract resolved · `3` HALT-for-human · `2` internal error.
165 
166 1. **Project folder** (cwd) is the project proxy.
167 2. **Frozen docs** — locate + state back the *description*, *implementation
168    plan*, and *execution log*. Resolution is no-guess:
169    - an explicit `foreman.config.json` `{ "docs": {...} }` wins; else
170    - a case-insensitive heuristic glob over top-level `*.md`.
171    - **0 candidates for a role -> HALT (missing).** **>1 candidate -> HALT
172      (ambiguous; ask, never pick).** Foreman never guesses which file is the plan.
173 3. **Wave parsing** — waves are read from an explicit `## Wave N` heading
174    (`## Sprint N` / `## Section N` accepted as aliases) in the plan doc. Headings
175    inside code fences are ignored. Wave numbers must be **contiguous 1..N**.
176    - **No parseable wave structure -> HALT.** Foreman never infers wave boundaries.
177 4. **Test discovery** — the build+test (gate) command, from the plan first
178    (`test-command:` / `build-and-test:` / `gate-command:` line), else the project
179    manifest (`package.json` `scripts.test` -> `npm test`; `pyproject.toml` with
180    pytest -> `pytest`).
181    - **No ground-truth test command found -> HALT** ("no ground truth -> cannot gate").
182 5. **Project-DONE definition** — DONE = the last parsed wave GREEN (via the
183    orchestrator-run gate) **and** any plan-level acceptance gate met. Foreman
184    emits a final-state verdict and stops; it does **not** loop past the last wave.
185 6. **Budget** — `{max waves this run, max fix-iters/wave (default 4), max
186    wall-clock}`; the Workflow `budget` token target is a secondary guard. **(enforced as a hard pre-flight gate)**
187 7. **Ambiguity gate (the linchpin).** Before acting, each execute/review agent
188    must emit `answerable-from-frozen-docs: yes/no + cited plan line`. A `no` is a
189    **HALT** (§6.4), never an autonomous decision. This is what makes "no
190    babysitting" possible without scope creep. **(implemented: the execute/review
191    agent prompts emit the gate; the engine cannot weaken it.)**
192

195 ## §5 — Judge arbitration + the trusted ground-truth gate (reward-hacking fix)
196 
197 **Evidence precedence:** OBSERVED test/command output -> reproduced execution
198 data -> directly-read authoritative source -> theory/argument.
199 
200 - **The gate is run by the orchestrator, not by a sub-agent.** The deterministic
201   Workflow step executes the build+test command, captures exit code + stdout/stderr
202   to a **gate-artifact file that sub-agents cannot write**; the judge reads only
203   that artifact. Sub-agent-pasted "command output" in a wave log is **never** the
204   gate of record. (Closes the forge-the-output hole.) **(implemented in `bin/wave-engine.mjs` `runGate`)**
205 - **Anti-test-weakening:** snapshot the test inventory + assertion/skip count at
206   wave start. A wave that reduces test count/coverage or adds `skip`/`xfail`
207   without an explicit plan citation is an **automatic HALT**, not a downgradeable
208   finding.
209 - **Vacuous-GREEN guard:** if the GREEN gate does not execute any artifact this
210   wave changed (coverage-of-changed-files check), it is **not** a GO — HALT as
211   "gate proves nothing about this wave."
212 - **Judge rules:** a GREEN gate outranks reviewer prose; to block GREEN a
213   reviewer must produce a **failing repro command + output**. The orchestrator's
214   readiness guard may HALT on missing required tests; the judge may not override
215   passing real output with argument.
216 - **Current-wave readiness:** explicitly declared required test files (including
217   `**Deliverables:** ... Test file test/wNN-name.test.mjs with ids: ...`) must
218   exist after execute and before GO, including resume with a proven ledger.
219   Unrelated source fixes and an older passing suite do not meet this source gate.
220   Documentation, spec, example and fixture references are not test declarations.
221   The bounded declaration grammar accepts `Test file <path>` at a sentence or
222   semicolon clause start, after an optional bullet/Deliverables label, or following
223   an add/create/implement/write/deliver/provide directive or `Replace ... with`.
224   `required`/`new` modifiers are supported. Bare paths, including Deliverables
225   bullets, do not create required-test declarations; fenced examples are ignored.
226   A `[taxonomy:missing-required-tests]` halt supports `--resume --clear-halt --force`
227   to re-enter EXECUTE at iteration 0 while preserving the prior ledger. Missing
228   tests still HALT; fresh gate and review are required before GO. Without force,
229   clear-halt keeps the ordinary gate re-entry and cannot skip this readiness guard.
230 - **Anti-sycophancy:** reviewers run read-only, are prompted to **refute**, cite
231   `file:line` or `command+output`; a **BLOCKER requires >=2 independent reviewers
232   to agree**.
233 - **Finding identity:** every finding carries a stable id (`file:line + rule`);
234   convergence = zero open BLOCKER/MAJOR with verified closure; a fix that closes
235   A but opens B is tracked to prevent false convergence / oscillation.
236   The established wave-wide `wave-not-implemented` rule alone combines citations
237   across files; retain every original reviewer/repro and count each reviewer once.
238   Orchestrator-owned `.foreman/wave-N-review-I.json` records expected, completed
239   and failed seats, bounded originals, merged evidence and decision before elegance.
240   A round-specific copy preserves prior evidence when resume repeats an iteration.
241   A pending round has no approval; a degraded round names missing votes explicitly.
242

245 ## §5b — The DELTA-COVERAGE gate (`bin/delta-coverage-gate.mjs`, journal 0091)
246 
247 **A wave that adds a SURFACE and ships zero tests is a BLOCKER, not a nit.**
248 
249 Why this is its own gate: a green suite is not evidence that a wave is covered.
250 Foreman built a subsystem GREEN that delivered **8 HTTP routes, 13 functions and
251 ~670 lines with not one test file mentioning it** — and the existing suite stayed
252 green *precisely because* the new code was untested. So "0 tests for 670 new lines"
253 and "full coverage" produced the same verdict. Six real defects were found later,
254 by reading.
255 
256 **Enforced in engine (journal 0092):** after vacuous-GREEN passes and before
257 `finishGo`, `wave-engine.mjs` runs `checkDeltaCoverage` on the wave's changed
258 files + test-file text; writes `.foreman/wave-N-delta-coverage.json`; **HALTs**
259 when a surface is uncovered. Soft-skip only on unexpected throw (never silent
260 suppress of a real fail). Sibling of Crucible's property-gate emit (0080/0081).
261 
262 Run `checkDeltaCoverage({changedFiles, testMentions})` per wave:
263 
264 1. **Delta, not percentage.** The unit is *what this wave added*. A global coverage
265    % is gameable and stays comfortably green while an entire subsystem is bare —
266    which is exactly how this happened. An unrelated test in the same wave does not
267    satisfy the gate.
268 2. **Surfaces are:** HTTP routes, handlers, CLI verbs, persistence paths, frontend
269    entry points. Adding one obliges a test that *names* it.
270 3. **Honor the repo's own convention.** Where a repo has stub gates
271    (`tests/test_<subsystem>_<wave>.py`), a new subsystem without one is an
272    INCOMPLETE wave — check for the convention rather than assuming a global suite.
273 4. **Emit the wire-up assertions by default** for any wave adding routes (static
274    text checks, no server boot — roughly five tests): every route reaches a handler
275    that exists; every handler is reachable; every endpoint the frontend calls is
276    declared; every route carries its expected auth policy; each failure path returns
277    its documented status code and text.
278 5. **Failure-path tests assert the USER-VISIBLE TEXT,** not just a non-crash. The
279    recurring defect in this family of work is a *confident wrong answer* — "no
280    projects", "queue 0" — which a happy-path test cannot see.
281 6. **No fixed-rate poller against an endpoint that spawns a process** — it ships with
282    visibility gating and failure backoff, or it does not ship.
283 
284 ## §6 — Halt-for-human conditions (the only things that wake you)
285 
286 1. Budget / iter / wall-clock cap.
287 2. Verdict **NO-GO**.
288 3. **Non-convergence** (`MAX_ITERS`, default 4, no GO) — `git stash`/branch the
289    failed attempt and record the ref so the tree is left clean and recoverable.
290 4. **Ambiguity / new-requirement / plan-deviation** — any
291    `answerable-from-docs: no` (§4.7), or a wave diff with no traceable plan basis.
292    - **`PLAN-AMENDMENT-PROPOSAL` (sub-type).** When a build-time discovery shows
293      the *frozen plan itself* is wrong/incomplete for the current wave (an
294      assumption falsified, an API not behaving as the plan assumed) — distinct
295      from mere ambiguity above — a review/execute agent may attach a concrete
296      proposed resolution: a **proposed diff** to the plan doc **plus a rationale**.
297      This is **still a HALT** — no silent re-planning. Foreman records the proposal
298      in the checkpoint `pending_action` for one-click human approval; on approval +
299      resume the bounded amendment is applied (or recorded as applied) and the wave
300      continues. The human stays in the loop and must approve before any plan change
301      takes effect; the §4.7 ambiguity gate and every §5 guard are unchanged. F3
302      only attaches a resolution to a halt that would otherwise be bare.
303 5. **Unrecoverable error** — can't verify a load-bearing claim; repo in bad
304    state; an irreversible action's gates didn't both verify; invalid/torn
305    checkpoint on resume (§8).
306 6. **Test-integrity / vacuous-GREEN** halts (§5).
307 
308 On every halt: write the checkpoint (§8) with the **exact recommended next
309 action** in `pending_action`. In Phase 0, the `bin` CLIs signal a HALT with
310 **exit code 3** and a `HALT: <reason>` line on stderr.
311

314 ## §8 — State, durability, resume (zero context bloat)
315 
316 - Sub-agents communicate via **file paths**, never by dumping transcripts into
317   the orchestrator. **(implemented)**
318 - **Per-wave logs + gate artifact:** the orchestrator-written gate artifact is
319   `.foreman/wave-<n>-gate.json` (`written_by:"orchestrator"`); the judge reads
320   only that. **(implemented)**
321 - **Canonical checkpoint `foreman-checkpoint.json`** (project root). Schema
322   (implemented in `bin/foreman-lib.mjs`, exercised by `bin/checkpoint.mjs`):
323 
324   | field | type | notes |
325   |---|---|---|
326   | `plan_path` | string | absolute path to the plan doc |
327   | `current_wave` | number | 1..N |
328   | `total_waves` | number | parsed count |
329   | `intra_wave_step` | string | `execute`\|`review`\|`fix`\|`judge`\|`gate`\|`done` |
330   | `iteration` | number | fix<->review iteration within the wave |
331   | `reviewer_count` | number | default 2 |
332   | `budget_remaining` | object | `{waves, fix_iters, wall_clock_min}` |
333   | `last_verdict` | string\|null | `GO`\|`NO-GO`\|`HALT`\|null |
334   | `last_commit` | string\|null | HEAD at last checkpoint |
335   | `open_findings` | array | `[{id, severity, file, line, rule, status}]` |
336   | `pending_action` | string\|null | exact recommended next action on halt |
337   | `stash_ref` | string\|null | non-convergence stash/branch ref |
338   | `status` | string | `running`\|`halted`\|`done` |
339 
340 - **Atomic writes:** serialize -> write `<file>.tmp` -> `fsync` -> atomic
341   `rename` over the destination. A torn write can never replace a valid file.
342 - **On resume, if the JSON is invalid (torn) or breaches the schema -> HALT.**
343   Never best-effort-parse a torn file.
344 - **Resume reconciliation (Phase 2):** compare `git rev-parse HEAD` to
345   checkpoint `last_commit`; if HEAD is ahead, adopt HEAD and skip the re-commit
346   (prevents double-apply). Intra-wave resume uses `intra_wave_step`.
347 
348 CLI (Phase 0):
349 
350 ```
351 node foreman/bin/checkpoint.mjs new <file> --plan <path> --waves <N> [--reviewers K]
352 node foreman/bin/checkpoint.mjs read <file>          # HALT (exit 3) on torn/invalid
353 node foreman/bin/checkpoint.mjs roundtrip <file> --plan <path> --waves <N>
354 node foreman/bin/checkpoint.mjs dashboard <file>     # render §10 block
355 ```

371 ## Files in this skill
372 
373 **Engine (Node — the orchestrator + gate live here, never in a sub-agent):**
374 - `bin/foreman-lib.mjs` — parsers + state primitives: `locateDocs`, `parseWaves`,
375   `discoverTestCommand`, `projectDoneDefinition`, checkpoint schema + atomic
376   `writeCheckpointAtomic`/`readCheckpoint`, `makeBudget`, `renderDashboard`.
377   Recoverable refusals throw `HaltError`.
378 - `bin/wave-engine.mjs` — the one-wave engine (`runWave`): EXECUTE -> orchestrator
379   GATE -> sequential REVIEWERS -> JUDGE -> bounded FIX -> re-gate, with all §5
380   guards (real-tests-ran GREEN predicate, anti-weakening, vacuous-GREEN, finding
381   identity). Language-aware gate for Node `--test` and `python -m pytest -v`.
382 - `bin/project-engine.mjs` — multi-wave auto-advance (`runProject`): ascending
383   truth-gated advance, project-DONE, budget pre-flight, wave/intra-wave/git resume.
384 - `bin/delta-coverage-gate.mjs` — §5b: classifies a wave's changed files, flags any
385   SURFACE (route / handler / CLI verb / persistence path / frontend entry) that no
386   test names, and returns a **BLOCKER**. Pure predicates over a file list — no git
387   spawn. `renderDeltaCoverageRequirement()` emits the wave text. **Wired into the
388   live GO path** in `wave-engine.mjs` (journal **0092**).
389 - `bin/git-hygiene.mjs` — §9 git hygiene: dedicated work branch, commit-only-on-GO,
390   dirty-tree HALT, repo-boundary containment, crash reconciliation. Never pushes.
391 - `bin/wave-workflow.js` — the production driver seam: `makeAgentDriver({agent})`
392   turns an injected `agent()` (Workflow `agent()`, the Agent tool, or a headless
393   `claude -p` child) into the engine's {execute, review, fix} steps.
394 - `bin/drivers/scripted-driver.mjs` — deterministic no-LLM driver used by the tests.
395 - `bin/locate-plan.mjs`, `bin/checkpoint.mjs`, `bin/run-wave.mjs`,
396   `bin/run-project.mjs` — CLIs (contract resolver, checkpoint IO, single-wave and
397   whole-project runners).
398 
399 **Why a Node process, not a Workflow script (design finding L):** a Workflow-tool
400 script has no filesystem/process access, but §5 requires the orchestrator to spawn
401 the test command and write a gate artifact sub-agents cannot forge. So the
402 orchestrator + gate + state live in this Node engine; the Workflow tool / sub-agents
403 drive only the model steps via the `agent()` seam.
404 
405 **Tests & fixtures:** `test/*.test.mjs` (106 passing), `fixtures/canonical-project/`
406 (Node, ships red), `fixtures/py-canonical/` (pytest, ships red), and the

409 ## How to invoke
410 
411 > **⏱ STATUS UPDATES TO CHAT — the launch pattern that makes the 10-min rule actually fire
412 > (2026-07-11 fix).** A Foreman build runs for hours. If a driving session launches the engine as a
413 > BLOCKING foreground call, the session is frozen for the whole run and CANNOT post updates — that is
414 > why status cadence silently goes dark. So whenever a Claude session drives a build:
415 > 1. **Launch the engine in the BACKGROUND** (Bash `run_in_background: true` — or `go.ps1` spawned
416 >    detached), NEVER a foreground call. The launch returns immediately and the session stays free.
417 > 2. **Arm the cadence at launch** — `ScheduleWakeup` (~600s) or `/loop 10m`, the moment the run starts.
418 > 3. **Each tick, relay — shell-free:** the engine writes the LOCKED Status table to
419 >    `<projectDir>/_foreman-status.log` at t=0, every ~10 min, and on halt/done. READ its tail with the
420 >    Read tool (never spawn a shell) and POST the latest status to chat in the LOCKED Status-table format —
421 >    canonical definition in ONE place: the canonical `AGENTS.md` → "Long-run progress updates"
422 >    (`[HH:MM]` header · Effort/Doing/Status/Tests/Blocker/Procs/**Journal** rows · ETA + To do footer).
423 >    The **Journal** row (mandatory, `none` when empty) recaps everything journaled since the last tick —
424 >    the engine log is the data source; the SESSION composes the Journal row from `journal/`.
425 >    The chat window is the PRIMARY channel (global AGENTS.md); the log is the data source.
426 > 4. **Stop the cadence** when the checkpoint `status` flips to `halted`/`done`, or the background task
427 >    notifies completion. The engine's own timer is the fallback if the session misses a tick — but only
428 >    the session can reach chat, so the background+relay pattern is mandatory, not optional.
429 
430 1. **Resolve the contract first.** From the project folder, run
431    `node <skill>/bin/locate-plan.mjs .`. If it prints `HALT:` (exit 3), fix the
432    named problem (add the missing doc, add `## Wave N` headings, declare a
433    `test-command:`) and re-invoke — Foreman never proceeds on a guessed contract.
434 2. **Dry-run the engine deterministically** (no LLM, reproducible) with the
435    scripted driver: `node <skill>/bin/run-project.mjs <projectDir>` (add `--git`
436    for commit-on-GO, `--max-waves`/`--max-wallclock-sec` for a budget cap,
437    `--resume` to continue from a checkpoint).
438 3. **Drive it with live sub-agents** using the robust wrapper script:
439    `powershell -File <skill>/bin/go.ps1 -Project <projectDir> [-Resume]`
440    The script automatically handles stale locks and executes through the backend registry (every subscription driver: `claude`, `chatgpt-cli`, `grok-cli`, `gemini-cli`). Seats come from the **Anchor dashboard** (`coding_family` → execute/fix, `review_family` → review; Anchor data-dir `settings.json` → `~/.anchor/model_prefs.json`) — a `TRIO_DRIVER` env is a per-run override, never the source. The wrapper also requires `$env:CRUCIBLE_AGENT_LIVE="1"` to allow live billable agents.
441 4. **Per-role model routing (the coding family codes, the review family reviews — whatever the dashboard selects; 2026-09-04).**
442    The dashboard prefs seat every role by default. To pin MODELS per role for one project, add a `"models"` block to the project's `foreman.config.json` (the example shows a gemini review seat; use the driver of the family the dashboard selects):
443    ```json
444    { "models": { "execute": "claude:claude-fable-5", "fix": "claude:claude-fable-5", "review": "gemini-cli:gemini-3.1-pro" } }
445    ```
446    `run-live.mjs` exports each entry as per-role env (`CLAUDE_MODEL_<ROLE>` for claude;
447    `TRIO_DRIVER_<ROLE>` + `TRIO_MODEL_<ROLE>` for another backend) and both driver
448    ladders resolve them (`resolveClaudeModel` / `resolveGeminiModel`; explicit env
449    always wins over config). The run header logs the resolved routing
450    (`model routing: execute=… · review=… · fix=…`) and every call's served model is
451    attested per SR-5 — check both when verifying a routing change.
452 
453 ## Standing rules (sleep-cycle promotion 2026-08-15 — journals 0093/0099/0100/0101)
454 
455 - **A GO with `last_commit: null` HALTs.** The EXECUTION-LOG append is part of
456   the GO transaction, not a courtesy; a checkpoint from a foreign project is
457   refused, never adopted; the gate refutes the reviewer — a reviewer verdict
458   that contradicts the orchestrator gate loses. (0093)
459 - **A test that enters through a different door than the human proves the
460   wrong thing.** §5b proves a new surface HAS a test; it does not prove the
461   surface is REACHABLE from the user's entry point — check reachability when
462   the wave's deliverable is user-facing. (0099, open engine work)
463 - **`--clear-halt` clears a STATE, not a defect.** Its refusal check is a
464   regex on halt text, not proof the remedy landed — clearing without landing
465   the named remedy re-buys the same halt. (0100)
466 - **The gate command must be a TEST RUNNER that emits counts.** A declared
467   gate that cannot count tests gates nothing; name the remedy in the halt
468   text. (0088 crucible / 0101)
469 
470 ## Usage journal (sleep-loop feed — append after every REAL run)
471 
472 At the end of any real (non-test) run of this skill, append ONE entry to
473 `journal/` in this skill folder as `NNNN-<slug>.md` (next number = **max(existing NNNN)+1 over the WHOLE directory** — gandalf accumulated 32 colliding ids because sessions read the low numbers as the frontier; APPEND-ONLY —
474 a correction is a new entry, never an edit). Keep it under ~15 lines, honest over
475 polished, with the 7 canonical fields (see the Skill Foundry's
476 `planning/portfolio-program/src/journal.mjs`): id, skill, situation, context,
477 observation, outcome (worked | friction | failed | refused), provenance
478 (genuine-execution | seeded — only genuine-execution corroborates).
479 No journal entries → the sleep loop has nothing to learn from.

482 record to `journal/runs/<ts>.json` AUTOMATICALLY at the end of every run (project, params,
483 per-wave outcomes, halt reason, tier, duration — the AGENTS.md "Run capture" standard) and
484 emits the LOCKED global Status table to the status log at t=0, every ~10 min, and at
